_comment: The sg-succession subject sidecar: Singapore's succession trio, encoded as
ONE subject against one shared ontology. See NOTES.md for why that is not
three subjects, and for the two L4 traps this corpus paid for.
THIS IS THE FIRST SUBJECT TO USE 'corpus.modules'. Before it, a descriptor
could name corpus.main plus an optional corpus.wizard and nothing else --
which cannot express an ontology module plus three statute modules plus a
case suite. The modules are listed IN DEPENDENCY ORDER: the domain module
declares the types the three Act modules import, sg-succession composes
them, and the case suite exercises the composition.
'checks.min_dated_arms' is 0 ON PURPOSE. This corpus carries NO rule-version
axis: it states the law as at the source bundle's in-force date (18 Aug
2026) and has no 'RULES EFFECTIVE DATE' arms at all. A 0 floor makes
p3-check report the temporal-closure sub-check NOT CHECKED rather than
vacuously green over an empty matched set. Raise it the day the corpus gains
dated arms; never lower a floor to make a run pass.
'checks.min_assertions' is 178 = the assertions_total that 'l4 run --json'
reports across the module set. The floor exists because 'no failed
assertion' is satisfied vacuously by an empty results[].
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-20, per module, via etc/go/lib/assert-report.mjs over
`l4 run --json` envelopes: sg-wills 62 + sg-paa 79 + sg-succession-cases 37
= 178, with 0 failed. The other four modules contribute none -- including
sg-isa, whose section 7 distribution rules are exercised entirely from
sg-succession-cases.l4 rather than in place.
This comment previously read '131 = ... (sg-wills 39 + sg-paa 55 + cases
37)', which was both stale against the declared 178 AND wrong in its own
arithmetic for the corpus as it then stood. It was left behind when the
corpus grew; the declared floor was updated and the sentence explaining it
was not, which is the drift that makes a comment worse than no comment.
'denovo' declares the three REGISTERS only, and deliberately declares
NEITHER 'modules' NOR 'surface_map'. SPEC.md section 8's diff oracle
compares a de novo encoding against a committed one; there is no prior
Singapore succession encoding, so there is nothing to diff, and a de novo
module that IS the corpus makes the comparison an identity (which the
resolver refuses). The registers are genuine P1/P2/P4 deposits regardless,
so 'go.sh run --milestone g2' validates them and p8-diff reports SKIPPED
with a named reason. See NOTES.md.
display_name: Singapore succession — Wills, Intestate Succession, Probate and Administration
citation: Wills Act 1838; Intestate Succession Act 1967; Probate and Administration Act 1934 (Singapore)
